# Niche examples: how to add them

*Generated by `build/build.py` (2026-10-17). The prompt list at the end is always current.*

The Niche level of the map shows real, public examples (papers, companies, products, pre-clinical and clinical work), each linked to the prompts it speaks to. They live in one spreadsheet, `curation/niche_examples.csv`, which Rethink Matters keeps.

## What counts

- A paper, preprint, company, product, or pre-clinical or clinical candidate that is **publicly documented**, with a public link.
- Not: anything known only from a session, unpublished results, private documents or decks, anything under an NDA, rumours, or personal contacts.

## The Chatham House Rule still applies

- Public facts only. Never record who suggested a row, and never connect a row to what anyone said in a session.
- No people's names in any column (paper titles are fine; leave out author lists).
- **The whole file is public on GitHub**, including the `notes` column, even though the site does not show notes.

## Adding rows in Excel

1. Open `curation/niche_examples.csv` in Excel. Add one row per example. Do not change or add column headings.
2. Save with **File, Save As, "CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited)"**, same name, and keep the CSV format when asked. (Plain "CSV" also works; the build converts it.)
3. Never save it as `.xlsx` in the project folder (the safety check refuses Excel files), and close Excel before building.

## The columns

| column | required | what to write |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | no | a short name for the example, lower case with hyphens (e.g. `example-paper-2021`). Left blank, it is made from the name; fill it in to keep links stable. |
| `type` | yes | one of `paper` (Paper), `preclinical` (Pre-clinical), `clinical` (Clinical), `product` (Product), `company` (Company), `other` (Other) |
| `name` | yes | its public name or the paper's title |
| `organisation` | no | the company, lab or journal |
| `year` | no | year of publication, founding, launch or trial start (four digits) |
| `stage` | no | how far along it is, in its own source's words (e.g. research, prototype, on the market, phase 1) |
| `summary` | no | one plain line: what it is or does, as its public source says. No opinions or 'first/best' claims. |
| `url` | yes | a public link: a DOI for papers, the organisation's own site, or a trial registry. Links into private storage (Google Drive or Docs, SharePoint, Dropbox, iCloud and the like), shortened links, signed links and local addresses are refused. |
| `prompts` | yes | the prompt(s) it speaks to, separated by `;`. Use the prompt id from the table below, the prompt's exact name, or paste the address of its Niche (it contains `focus=n:` and the id). |
| `status` | yes | `draft` when added; `checked` once a second person has checked it; `hidden` to withdraw it. **Only `checked` rows appear on the map.** |
| `notes` | no | notes for the checker. Public on GitHub, not shown on the map. |

## Checking a row (two different people)

The person who adds a row sets `draft`. A second person opens the link in a private window and confirms that it is public, that the summary matches the source, that the stage is stated by the source, that the prompt fits, and that nothing comes from a session; then they set `checked`.

## What the build checks

Every row needs a type, name, public link, at least one known prompt and a status. Problems are reported by spreadsheet row (the header is row 1), with suggestions for misspelled prompts. Rows that start with `#` and empty rows are skipped, but every cell of every row, parked ones included, is checked for private links and e-mail addresses, because the whole file is public.
